newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss asset manager Baer says 1997 starts well.
newsitem.headline: Swiss asset manager Baer says 1997 starts well.

text.p: Swiss asset management and private banking group Julius Baer Holding AG said on Tuesday 1997 had started very well and forecast positive development this year after boosting net profit by 16 percent in 1996.
"Results in the first two months of the current year were very good in all areas," the bank said in a statement released before a news conference.
It said the group, one of Europe's few quoted fund management specialists, expected continued positive development in 1997.

Baer reported on January 31 that 1996 group net profit rose 16 percent to 134 million Swiss francs ($90.9 million). Assets under management, the key to Baer's future earnings power, jumped 29 percent to 63.6 billion Swiss francs ($43.1 billion).
Chief executive Rudolf Baer said the group was considering buying back shares but had not made a decision.

"We are considering various creative possibilities at the moment but I cannot say anything definitive today about how we will proceed," Baer said in the text of a speech released before a news conference.
Baer said there were still tax reasons that militated against a buy-back of shares. He said talks were going on with tax authorities.

Baer said in January it planned to raise its dividend on 1996 results by 18 percent to 39 francs per bearer share from 33 francs and to 7.80 francs per registered share from 6.60 francs. ($ = 1.474 Swiss Francs)
